page: Amazon Web Services r6a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro system. The configuration provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores and 32 threads, driven by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at speeds up to 3.6 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 256 GB of DDR4 system RAM operating at 3 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Processor cache provisions comprise 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Cryptographic hardware instructions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI are supported, while extended vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX are not present.

The r6a.8xlarge instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring all persistent storage volumes to be attached across the network via Amazon Elastic Block Store. Network capacity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps. The absence of physical NVMe disks limits zero-latency disk caching and increases dependency on network-attached storage bandwidth. In addition, the lack of AVX-512 extensions and dedicated GPU accelerators restricts throughput for heavy matrix workloads, as observed in low token throughput during 70B parameter model prompt processing tests.

Standardized benchmark testing shows strong results for single-core processor workloads, hardware-assisted encryption, and memory operations. Multi-core compute performance, web serving, and Redis key-value operations fall within typical mid-tier ranges. From a resource perspective, the high memory density per compute core on AMD EPYC architecture offers efficient memory capacity without excessive CPU overprovisioning. The r6a.8xlarge is suited for in-memory caching solutions, mid-to-large relational databases, distributed state stores, and memory-intensive ETL tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r6a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at 3.6 GHz, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 256 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz. The instance does not include local disk storage, depending on network-attached storage for persistence, and provides a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark measurements indicate strong performance in single-core compute, cryptographic routines, and memory scores, alongside average throughput in multi-core metrics, decompression tasks, and Redis operations. The lack of AVX-512 instruction sets and local NVMe storage limits its utility for specialized vector processing and fast scratchpad I/O. The r6a.8xlarge is suited for memory-intensive workloads including Redis clusters, in-memory databases, and large enterprise application state handling.
